column1: # One-hex displacements, applied after port_place.tsv is mapped onto the grid.
# A hex is 5 degrees, and some harbours are closer together than that. Kochi
# and Colombo, Palma and Algiers, Genoa and Marseille, Pisa and Naples, Lisbon
# and Seville, Acapulco and Veracruz all land in the same cell, and two ports
# in one hex cannot both be drawn or both be sailed to. Nudging is the honest
# way out: the grid is the constraint, so say which port was moved and why,
# rather than quietly rounding a coordinate until the clash disappears.
# In each pair the port moved is the one that really does lie in that direction
# from the other, so the map stays right about their relative positions even
# where it cannot be right about both absolute ones. Two of these are moved for
# a second reason as well: Veracruz and Seville each end up on the coast the
# port is actually on, which the unnudged cell got wrong.
# scripts/gen_game_data.py fails the build on any collision it is not given a
# nudge for, so this file cannot silently fall out of date with the map.
# dcol and drow are offsets in odd-r offset coordinates.
